shape.description: Hollow yellow body, tapered: about one cell square at a foot band, narrowing upward, on four short block-style legs. Three sides have an arched opening down to a shared low bowl floor: the front and both flanks. The rear wall is solid. The bowl floor has a round hole in its centre, smaller than a marble. On top a long curved orange seesaw lever pivots on a pin through the upper body (screw visible on each side). Its long tail, with a double-arrow mark, sticks out about 0.7 cell behind the rear wall and rests raised; its short nose ends just past the front wall. Under the lever a toothed section enters a slot in the top. A yellow tongue with a small arrow mark hangs at the top of the front arch, directly over the outlet, with a row of small teeth under it.
shape.sizeBasis: Estimated, not measured: cell about 62 mm and slot about 47 mm, from block width against a hand and marbles (IMG_0951, IMG_0952) and the plan drawing proportion slot/cell about 0.76. src/catalog/parts.js uses a 50 mm cell, also an estimate. Ratios to cell and slot are better known than the millimetres.

accepts: a finger pressing the tail down

physics.behaviour: A marble rolling in through either flank arch settles in the low bowl and waits at the front outlet, under the yellow tongue. It does not fall through the hole: the hole is narrower than the marble and acts as a seat. Pressing the raised lever tail down pivots the lever, and its toothed section drives the mechanism behind the tongue, which shoves the marble out of the front. It is a holding point as well as a launcher, and two tracks can merge into it. The launch is strong enough to climb M-10 and jump to M-11.

evidence.shows: Flank view, M-01 stacked on B-04 on B-01. Curved lever, side pin, tail raised. Flank arch open, orange T-02 clipped to the bowl rim, round hole in the bowl floor with light showing through. T-06 leaves the front under a yellow tongue. Rear wall solid.
Front view: T-06 clips into the bowl under the yellow tongue with its row of teeth; lever tail above with chevrons pointing to the outlet; orange tracks visible at both flanks.
Rear three-quarter view: lever pivot and toothed section entering the top slot; T-02 mating on the near flank, another orange track on the far flank, rear face plain.
The yellow-and-orange lever piece pushes marbles toward the rocket and can be fed by two tracks.
Two orange curves reach the box, one per flank; the blue T-06 leaves the front toward M-10; a gold marble sits at the outlet. The piece stands raised on a stack, not on the floor.
Placement 1: M-12 low end enters one flank; T-06 leaves the front to the low end of M-10. M-01 stands on the floor at the front corner of the long edge. The other flank window is empty.
Placement 2: M-01 at cell B7, T-06 leaves west at B6 to M-10 at B4-B5. Lever and arrows point west toward the outlet; lever tail overhangs B8. Nothing feeds it in Part 3 itself.
Part named M-01 with label 14 on the body.
Underside view shows a one-cell body with the lever hinged to it.
Tall tapered yellow housing on block feet, flank and front arches over a bowl, small hood over the front arch, long thick orange paddle lever pivoting near the front with its tail raised behind

assumptions: Origin at footprint centre at foot level (the top plane of whatever the piece stands on). East is +x, south is +y, z in slots.

Port height 0.75 slot: IMG_0962 shows the bowl floor about 0.6 slot above the leg feet, and T-06 runs about level to the M-10 low seat at 0.75 in step 3-4. Estimated, not measured. It replaces the 1 slot first read from the drawing's window.
Hole narrower than the marble is judged from photos: hole about 125 px against a marble about 170 px at the same depth, scaled from the channel width. The marble was not tested on it.
Which part strikes the marble is inferred: the toothed lever section and the tongue teeth suggest a geared hammer, but no photo shows the inside. The tongue may instead be a keeper that lifts away.
Inlet to outlet are assumed to share one bowl, since all three arches open onto it (IMG_0962, IMG_0963).
openQuestions: Drop a marble on the hole with M-01 lifted off the floor: does it stay in the bowl?
Press slowly with the marble seated: does the tongue swing forward, or does something behind the marble move?
Can the front arch accept an inlet, or a flank arch act as an outlet?
Do two marbles waiting from the two flanks jam, or queue?
How far does a full press send a marble on the flat?
